# New-ZbxServiceProblemTag

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a service problem tag for the -ProblemTag of New-ZbxService and Set-ZbxService.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxServiceProblemTag [-Tag] <string> [-Operator <ZabbixServiceProblemTagOperator>] [-Value <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A problem tag links a service to the problems that carry a matching tag, so they set the service's status. The New-ZbxServiceProblemTag cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -ProblemTag of New-ZbxService and Set-ZbxService take as it is, alone or in an array. -Tag is positional. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build a problem tag and use it in a new service

```powershell
$tag = New-ZbxServiceProblemTag -Tag 'service' -Operator Equal -Value 'checkout'
New-ZbxService -Name 'Checkout' -Algorithm MostCritical -Position 0 -ProblemTag $tag | Select-Object Name, Status
```

The builder writes one problem-tag hashtable (tag, operator, value); New-ZbxService sends it in -ProblemTag. The service then takes its status from problems tagged service=checkout.

### Example 2: Match several tags, one with a pattern

```powershell
$tags = @(
    New-ZbxServiceProblemTag -Tag 'service' -Operator Equal -Value 'checkout'
    New-ZbxServiceProblemTag -Tag 'env' -Operator Like -Value 'prod'
)
$null = Set-ZbxService -InputObject 'Checkout' -ProblemTag $tags
(Get-ZbxService -Name 'Checkout' -SelectProblemTags).ProblemTags | Format-Table Tag, Operator, Value
```

-Operator Like matches when the problem's tag value contains the text. Several tags in -ProblemTag must all match.
